behavior: An opportunistic omnivore that forages while walking, swimming, or flying; takes food from land or the water’s surface, sometimes plunge-dives, steals from other birds, scavenges, and drops hard-shelled prey onto rocks to break it open.
field_marks: Large, robust body with broad, pointed wings
Heavy bill; yellow with a red spot in adults, dark in young birds
Pale eyes and dull pink legs in adults
Breeding adults have a white head and underparts with a pale-gray back; nonbreeding adults have gray-brown or dusky streaking on the head and neck
Black adult wingtips show small white spots
Immatures are mottled brown, with a dark tail band when young
habitat: Occupies water-associated habitats including coasts, bays, beaches, open water, mudflats, lakes, major rivers, marshes, fields, docks, and refuse sites. It commonly nests on islands or other open ground and sometimes on gravel roofs.

measurements.length: 56–66 cm (22 in–2 ft 2 in), sexes similar
measurements.weight: 800–1,250 g (1 lb 12 oz–2 lb 12 oz), sexes similar
measurements.wingspan: 120–150 cm (3 ft 11 in–4 ft 11 in), sexes similar
